# Snatch.auction (urlsnatcher.com)

Live site: **https://urlsnatcher.com**

Snatch.auction is a Domain Fetch and Domain Creation platform.

## What the product does

- Interprets a natural-language business brief.
- Scans live NameSilo auction inventory.
- Generates candidate names when auction supply is insufficient.
- Verifies generated names through live NameSilo registration availability.
- Returns ranked Decision Candidates with fit reasoning, risk, tradeoffs, and action paths.

## Decision Candidate model

A Decision Candidate is inventory enriched with:

- verified live status (`statusVerifiedAt`, `statusExpiresAt`)
- source (`namesilo-auction`, `namesilo-available`, `namesilo-premium`)
- acquisition path (`register`, `auction`, `buy-now`, `make-offer`, `verify`)
- score dimensions (semantic fit, buyer fit, brandability, pronounceability, category clarity, tld trust, friction, signal, risk, overall)
- explanations (why surfaced, best-if, less-ideal-if, catch, next action)

## Public discovery surfaces

### Search engines (URL discovery only)

Submit **only** `https://urlsnatcher.com/sitemap.xml` to Google Search Console.

That index points to XML urlsets only (`sitemap-core.xml`, `sitemap-intents.xml`, `sitemap-domains-indexed.xml`).

Do **not** submit NDJSON/JSON feed URLs as sitemaps. Feeds are machine-readable inventory infrastructure, not sitemap documents.

### AI systems and programmatic clients (feed discovery)

Expose and link these endpoints everywhere:

| Feed | NDJSON | JSON | Landing page |
|------|--------|------|----------------|
| Public listings (default `scope=indexed`) | `/api/domain-listings.ndjson` | `/api/domain-listings.json` | `/data/domain-listings` |
| Full durable catalog | `/api/domain-feed.ndjson` | `/api/domain-feed.json` | `/data/domain-feed` |
| Marketplace graph export | `/api/domain-graph.ndjson` | — | `/data/domain-graph` |
| Per-domain graph | — | `/api/domains/{slug}/graph.json` | `/domains/{slug}` |

Dataset metadata JSON: `/api/domain-listings.dataset.json`

Feed landing pages include Dataset + DataFeed schema, record counts, update policy, field lists, and example records.

Homepage injects Dataset schema plus `<link rel="alternate" type="application/x-ndjson">` discovery tags for all three feeds.

Domain product pages link per-domain graph JSON and the public listings feed.

### Graph export node types

`/api/domain-graph.ndjson` emits entity/relationship lines per domain:

- Nodes: `Domain`, `Offer`, `Auction`, `Category`, `UseCase`, `Provider`, `TLD`, `Intent`, `Persona`, `ComparableDomain`
- Edges: `hasOffer`, `listedInAuction`, `inCategory`, `supportsUseCase`, `hasIntent`, `targetsPersona`, `listedWith`, `relatedTo`, `soldBy`

Future entity pages (not implemented yet): `/categories/{slug}`, persona pages, category↔domain↔use-case interlinks.

### Feed delivery headers

Candidate pages: `/domains/:slug`

### Public listing feeds (inline, not forced download)

Browser navigation (normal address-bar visits) renders an HTML preview page for feed URLs. API clients and curl still receive feed bytes directly.

- Default NDJSON delivery: `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` with `X-Feed-Format: application/x-ndjson` so browsers display inline instead of downloading unknown MIME types.
- Strict NDJSON MIME: add `?view=raw` or `?raw=1`, or send `Accept: application/x-ndjson`.

- Public listing feed (NDJSON): `/api/domain-listings.ndjson`
  - Default: `scope=indexed` (index-now / sitemap-aligned active listings)
  - `scope=active` — all active auction product pages, including hold-noindex
  - `scope=archive` — ended/sold/unavailable records
  - Headers: `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: inline`
- Public listing feed (JSON): `/api/domain-listings.json` — same records as NDJSON, default `limit=1000`
  - Headers: `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: inline`

### Full internal catalog feeds

- Full durable catalog feed (NDJSON): `/api/domain-feed.ndjson` — all durable records with full graph payloads
- Full durable catalog feed (JSON): `/api/domain-feed.json` — internal catalog JSON, default `limit=1000`

### Marketplace graph export

- Graph export (NDJSON): `/api/domain-graph.ndjson` — marketplace graph nodes/edges for AI retrieval
  - Node types: Domain, Offer, Auction, Category, UseCase, Provider, TLD, Intent, Persona, ComparableDomain
  - One `MarketplaceGraphRecord` line per durable domain record

### Dataset / DataFeed metadata

- Feed catalog metadata: `/api/domain-listings.dataset.json`
  - Schema.org Dataset describing listings, catalog, and graph feeds

## Sitemaps and SEO tiers (verified implementation)

Submit **only** `https://urlsnatcher.com/sitemap.xml` in Google Search Console.

Do **not** submit HTML page URLs (for example `/experiments/intent-fetch/` or `/experiments/auction-radar/`) as sitemaps — those are regular pages listed inside `sitemap-core.xml`, not sitemap files. If GSC shows "Sitemap is HTML" for a page URL, remove that submission and keep only `/sitemap.xml`.

Valid sitemap endpoints (XML only):

- `/sitemap.xml` — sitemap index (submit this one)
- `/sitemap-core.xml` — core static pages urlset
- `/sitemap-intents.xml` — published intent pages urlset
- `/sitemap-domains-indexed.xml` — index-now domain product pages urlset

`/robots.txt` points to `/sitemap.xml` only.

### SEO tier model (source: `server/candidate-store/seo-tier.js`)

Every NameSilo auction durable record gets a full product page at `/domains/{slug}`. Tier controls indexing exposure, not page existence.

| Tier | Robots | In domain sitemap | Notes |
|------|--------|-------------------|-------|
| `index-now` | `index,follow` | yes | Product + Offer JSON-LD, graph linked, bare canonical |
| `hold-noindex` | `noindex,follow` | no | Default for new ingests; eligible for batch promotion |
| `archive` | `noindex` | no | Ended, sold, or unavailable auctions |

Sitemap inclusion filter (`listSitemapCandidates`): lifecycle active, `index-now` tier, fresh `statusExpiresAt`, passes full `validateIndexNowEligibility`, bare canonical (no `?`), product graph + Product/Offer schema complete.

Domain sitemap `lastmod` order: `statusVerifiedAt`, then `updatedAt`, `publishedAt`, `createdAt` (ISO 8601).

Promotion gate (`validateIndexNowEligibility`): active auction, fresh `statusExpiresAt`, valid canonical and NameSilo acquisition URL, quality score ≥ 55, no gibberish/spam/excessive-length flags, Product + Offer schema complete, category/use-case signals present.

### Rollout tooling

- Audit: `node scripts/audit-indexing-candidates.js`
- Verify strategy: `node scripts/verify-sitemap-strategy.js`
- Batch promote: `node scripts/promote-index-tier.js --limit=500 --dry-run` then without `--dry-run`
- Refresh auction status before promotion: `node scripts/ingest-namesilo-auctions.js --write --start-page=1 --end-page=125`

Expand index tier in batches (500 → 2,000 → 5,000 → 10,000) only after GSC crawl/index signals look healthy. Do not index all durable records at once.

### Current batch state (verify live)

Run `node scripts/verify-sitemap-strategy.js` for current counts. Frozen QA manifest: `data/reports/index-batch-500-manifest-2026-06-12T19-29-50-048Z.json`.

Production deploy ships the frozen 500-record batch in `data/index-now-batch.json` (regenerate with `npm run export:index-now-batch` after promotion changes). Railway uses this when `data/product-records/` is absent. Server startup refreshes stale `statusExpiresAt` TTL for index-now batch records so the domain sitemap stays populated between ingests.

## Persistent APIs

- `POST /api/domain-fetch`
- `GET /api/candidates`
- `GET /api/candidates/:candidateId`
- `POST /api/compare-candidates`
- `POST /api/refine-candidates`
- `POST /api/shortlist-candidate`
- `POST /api/watch-auction`
- `POST /api/acquisition-path`

## Methodology and freshness

- Auction status should be refreshed near action time.
- Registration availability should be refreshed immediately before handoff.
- Stale candidates should be treated as pending verification.

## Acquisition behavior

- Snatch.auction prepares acquisition handoff links.
- Snatch.auction does not auto-purchase, auto-register, auto-bid, or auto-offer.
- Irreversible actions require explicit human confirmation.

## Safety and data handling

Never expose or log:

- NameSilo API keys
- account identifiers
- auth tokens
- private seller/account fields
